input.prompt:
You are writing a black-box test suite for a Logo interpreter in /work (a Bun + TypeScript project). Do NOT modify anything under /work/src. Only create test files under /work/tests/ (e.g. /work/tests/spec.test.ts, you may split into several *.test.ts files).

API under test: `import { run } from '../src/lang/index'` — `run(source: string, mode: '2d' | '3d')` returns `{ segments, error }` synchronously. `segments` is an array of `{ from: [x,y,z], to: [x,y,z], color: string /* lowercase #rrggbb */, width: number }` in drawing order; `error` is `null` or `{ message: string /* Polish */, line: number, column: number }` (1-based). On a parse-time error segments is empty; on a run-time error segments holds what was drawn before the error.

Run the tests with `cd /work && bun test tests`. Use `toBeCloseTo` for coordinates computed through trigonometry. Write thorough tests derived ONLY from the specification below (your own careful reading — do not read the implementation in /work/src to decide what the expected behaviour is). Cover: lexical rules (case-insensitivity, accented/unaccented aliases, comments, number formats incl. rejected `1e3`, `0x10`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, colour literals), every command and alias, expression precedence/associativity, the binary-operator whitespace rule (incl. `np 10 -5` error located at the `-`), unary signs, division by zero, exact comparisons, turtle geometry incl. 3D pitch/roll orientation semantics exactly as described, `dom`, `czyść`, repeat & `nrpowt` (incl. the lexical parse-time rule), variables & scoping (global vs local, shadowing, declared-name rule, unassigned-variable runtime error position), conditionals, procedures (both header forms, `:name` references, arg-count errors, recursion, `stop` semantics inside repeat/conditional bodies, definitions after use, duplicate definitions, definitions inside bodies, missing `już`), error positions (line/column rules for invalid/missing args), parse-time vs run-time behaviour (nothing drawn vs keep drawn), and every limit (characters, tokens, bracket nesting 32, frames 32, operations 10000 with the exact counting rule, segments 10000, coordinates ±100000). For the operation counting, the spec's rule is quoted below; where the spec is genuinely ambiguous (e.g. whether a body interrupted by `stop` counts as "finishing"), avoid asserting the ambiguous detail, and keep boundary tests to cases that are unambiguous. Messages are Polish but free-form: assert `error !== null` and line/column, never exact message text (you may assert the message is a non-empty string).

When done, run the suite. For every failing test, decide whether the test or the implementation is wrong by re-reading the spec. Fix tests that were wrong. Leave genuinely failing tests that reveal implementation bugs in place but ALSO mark them with `test.todo`-free normal `test` so they fail — then in your final report list each implementation bug: the program, the expected result per spec (quote the spec sentence), and the actual result. Keep the final report concise (a list), and state the final pass/fail counts.

=== SPECIFICATION (the language) ===

### Lexical rules

- Keywords, procedure names, variable names and parameter names ignore case. Accented Polish spellings listed below work alongside the unaccented ones.
- Whitespace separates tokens; newlines matter only for procedure headers and endings (see Procedures).
- A semicolon starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.
- Numbers are unsigned decimal literals: `80`, `12.5`, `.5`. A sign is an operator (see Expressions). Nothing else is a number: `1e3`, `0x10`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are errors.
- Square brackets `[` and `]` delimit repeat and conditional bodies and may nest. Parentheses `(` and `)` group expressions.
- A colour literal is a quoted six-digit hex string: `"#16866a"` (case-insensitive hex digits).
- The operators are `+ - * /`, the comparisons `< > = <= >= <>`.

### Commands

| Polish | English | Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `np`, `naprzod`, `naprzód` | `fd`, `forward` | expression | Move forward by that distance |
| `ws`, `wstecz` | `bk`, `back` | expression | Move backward |
| `pw`, `prawo` | `rt`, `right` | expression | Turn right by that many degrees |
| `lw`, `lewo` | `lt`, `left` | expression | Turn left by that many degrees |
| `pod`, `podnies`, `podnieś` | `pu`, `penup` | none | Raise the pen |
| `opu`, `opusc`, `opuść` | `pd`, `pendown` | none | Lower the pen |
| `kolor` | `color` | colour literal | Set the pen colour |
| `grubosc`, `grubość` | `width` | expression, integer 1–12 | Set the stroke width |
| `powtorz`, `powtórz` | `repeat` | expression, integer 0–10000, then `[ body ]` | Run the body that many times |
| `niech` | `let` | name, then expression | Assign a variable |
| `jeśli`, `jesli` | `if` | condition, then `[ body ]` | Run the body when the condition holds |
| `jeżeli`, `jezeli` | `ifelse` | condition, then `[ body ]` `[ body ]` | Run the first body when the condition holds, else the second |
| `stop` | `stop` | none | End the current procedure; at top level, end the program |
| `dom` | `home` | none | Return to the origin and the initial orientation |
| `czyść`, `czysc` | `cs`, `clearscreen` | none | Forget every drawn segment |
| `gora`, `góra` | `pitchup` | expression | Pitch the nose up by that many degrees (3D only) |
| `dol`, `dół` | `pitchdown` | expression | Pitch the nose down (3D only) |
| `pp`, `przechylprawo` | `rr`, `rollright` | expression | Roll to the right around the heading (3D only) |
| `pl`, `przechyllewo` | `rl`, `rollleft` | expression | Roll to the left (3D only) |

Every Polish and English alias is equivalent. `nrpowt` (alias `repcount`) is a value, not a command: see Repeat.

### Expressions

- Wherever a command takes an expression, it accepts a number, a name (a parameter or a variable, also in the legacy form `:name`), `nrpowt`, a parenthesised expression, a unary `-` or `+` applied to any of these, or two expressions joined by `+`, `-`, `*` or `/`.
- `*` and `/` bind tighter than `+` and `-`; operators of equal precedence associate to the left: `np 20 - 5 - 3` moves 12 and `np 2 + 3 * 4` moves 14.
- A binary operator must have whitespace on both sides or on neither side. `np 10 - 5` and `np 10-5` both move 5. `np 10 -5` is `np 10` followed by the stray token `-5`, which is an error, because the `-` has whitespace only on its left. The same rule applies to `+`, `*` and `/`. The rule does not apply to comparisons.
- Unary signs may be stacked and applied anywhere an operand is expected: `np -(3 - 5)`, `np - -2`, `np -bok`.
- Division by zero and any non-finite result are run-time errors. Evaluating an expression is not an executed operation (see Limits).
- A condition is `expression comparison expression`. Comparisons are exact: `jeśli 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 [...]` does not run its body.

### Turtle and geometry

- Coordinates are right-handed: +X to the right, +Y forward on the page, +Z up out of the page. The 2D plane is the XY plane (z = 0).
- The turtle starts at the origin (0, 0, 0), heading +Y, with its right side along +X and its up vector along +Z, pen down, colour `#16866a`, width 3.
- `np d` moves the turtle `d` units along its heading; `ws d` moves it `-d`. If the pen is down and the position changes, a straight segment from the old to the new position is drawn with the current colour and width. A move of zero draws nothing.
- `pw a` rotates the heading `a` degrees to the right around the turtle's up vector (clockwise when seen from above); `lw a` rotates left. The right vector follows the heading.
- `gora a` rotates the heading `a` degrees towards the up vector around the right vector (the up vector follows, so after `gora 90` the turtle heads along its former up); `dol a` rotates the opposite way.
- `pp a` rotates the turtle's up vector `a` degrees towards its right vector, around the heading (the right vector follows, so after `pp 90` the turtle's up is its former right and its right is its former down); `pl a` rotates the opposite way. The heading does not change.
- In 2D mode, `gora`, `dol`, `pp` and `pl` are errors.
- Angles are in degrees, any decimal value; negative values turn the other way.
- `dom` moves the turtle to the origin, drawing a segment if the pen is down and the turtle is not already there, then sets the heading to +Y, the right vector to +X and the up vector to +Z. Pen state, colour and width are untouched.
- `czyść` removes every segment drawn so far and changes nothing else: `run` then returns only the segments drawn afterwards. The segment limit (see Limits) counts the segments currently kept.
- Pen state, colour and width persist until changed. Programs made only of flat commands produce identical coordinates in 2D and 3D mode.

### Repeat

`powtorz n [ ... ]` runs the bracketed commands `n` times; `n` must evaluate to an integer from 0 to 10000 (0 runs nothing). Bodies may contain any commands, nested repeats, conditionals and procedure calls.

Inside a repeat body, `nrpowt` is the number of the current iteration of the innermost enclosing repeat, starting at 1. The enclosing repeat is found lexically: `nrpowt` written in a procedure body that is not itself inside a repeat is a parse-time error, even if the procedure is only ever called from inside a repeat. `nrpowt` written outside any repeat at top level is a parse-time error too.

### Variables

- `niech x 5` assigns the value of the expression to the variable `x`; any later `niech x ...` reassigns it. Variable names follow the rules for procedure names and may not be command words or the name of a procedure.
- A `niech` at top level creates or updates a global variable. A `niech` inside a procedure creates or updates a variable local to that call; it shadows a global of the same name for the rest of the call and is discarded when the call ends. A parameter can be reassigned the same way.
- A name may be used in an expression only if it is a parameter of the enclosing procedure, or is assigned by `niech` somewhere in the body of the enclosing procedure, or is assigned by `niech` somewhere at top level (before or after the use). Any other name is a parse-time error.
- Reading a declared variable that has not been assigned yet on the current path is a run-time error, reported at the first token of the argument that contains the reference.

### Conditionals

`jeśli warunek [ ... ]` runs the body when the condition holds. `jeżeli warunek [ ... ] [ ... ]` runs the first body when it holds and the second otherwise. Bodies may contain anything a repeat body may contain. Conditional bodies count towards the bracket nesting limit but are not execution frames.

### Procedures

```logo
oto kwadrat ma: bok, kąt
  powtorz 4 [np bok pw kąt]
już

kwadrat 80 90
```

- A definition starts with `oto` (alias `to`) at the beginning of a line, followed on the same line by the name and, optionally, `ma:` and a comma-separated parameter list. The body follows on the next lines and ends with `już` (aliases `juz`, `end`) alone on its own line.
- The legacy header `oto kwadrat :bok :kąt` is also accepted, and a parameter may be referenced in the body as `:bok` as well as plainly as `bok`.
- Calls take positional arguments separated by whitespace, exactly as many as the procedure has parameters; each argument is an expression, so `kwadrat 40 * 2 90` passes 80 and 90. A parameter may share its name with a procedure: in command position the name is a call, in argument position it is the parameter.
- Parameters and local variables are local to the call and can stand in for any expression, including repeat counts and arguments of other procedure calls.
- Definitions are top-level only (never inside a repeat body, a conditional body or another procedure) and may appear before or after the calls that use them. A name may be defined once.
- Procedures may call themselves, directly or through other procedures. `stop` ends the current call immediately; at top level it ends the program. A `stop` inside a repeat or conditional body ends the enclosing procedure call (or the program), not just the body.

For the operation counting, the spec's rule is quoted below; where the spec is genuinely ambiguous (e.g. whether a body interrupted by `stop` counts as "finishing"), avoid asserting the ambiguous detail, and keep boundary tests to cases that are unambiguous. Messages are Polish but free-form: assert `error !== null` and line/column, never exact message text (you may assert the message is a non-empty string).

When done, run the suite. For every failing test, decide whether the test or the implementation is wrong by re-reading the spec. Fix tests that were wrong. Leave genuinely failing tests that reveal implementation bugs in place but ALSO mark them with `test.todo`-free normal `test` so they fail — then in your final report list each implementation bug: the program, the expected result per spec (quote the spec sentence), and the actual result. Keep the final report concise (a list), and state the final pass/fail counts.

=== SPECIFICATION (the language) ===

### Lexical rules

- Keywords, procedure names, variable names and parameter names ignore case. Accented Polish spellings listed below work alongside the unaccented ones.
- Whitespace separates tokens; newlines matter only for procedure headers and endings (see Procedures).
- A semicolon starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.
- Numbers are unsigned decimal literals: `80`, `12.5`, `.5`. A sign is an operator (see Expressions). Nothing else is a number: `1e3`, `0x10`, `NaN` and `Infinity` are errors.
- Square brackets `[` and `]` delimit repeat and conditional bodies and may nest. Parentheses `(` and `)` group expressions.
- A colour literal is a quoted six-digit hex string: `"#16866a"` (case-insensitive hex digits).
- The operators are `+ - * /`, the comparisons `< > = <= >= <>`.

### Commands

| Polish | English | Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `np`, `naprzod`, `naprzód` | `fd`, `forward` | expression | Move forward by that distance |
| `ws`, `wstecz` | `bk`, `back` | expression | Move backward |
| `pw`, `prawo` | `rt`, `right` | expression | Turn right by that many degrees |
| `lw`, `lewo` | `lt`, `left` | expression | Turn left by that many degrees |
| `pod`, `podnies`, `podnieś` | `pu`, `penup` | none | Raise the pen |
| `opu`, `opusc`, `opuść` | `pd`, `pendown` | none | Lower the pen |
| `kolor` | `color` | colour literal | Set the pen colour |
| `grubosc`, `grubość` | `width` | expression, integer 1–12 | Set the stroke width |
| `powtorz`, `powtórz` | `repeat` | expression, integer 0–10000, then `[ body ]` | Run the body that many times |
| `niech` | `let` | name, then expression | Assign a variable |
| `jeśli`, `jesli` | `if` | condition, then `[ body ]` | Run the body when the condition holds |
| `jeżeli`, `jezeli` | `ifelse` | condition, then `[ body ]` `[ body ]` | Run the first body when the condition holds, else the second |
| `stop` | `stop` | none | End the current procedure; at top level, end the program |
| `dom` | `home` | none | Return to the origin and the initial orientation |
| `czyść`, `czysc` | `cs`, `clearscreen` | none | Forget every drawn segment |
| `gora`, `góra` | `pitchup` | expression | Pitch the nose up by that many degrees (3D only) |
| `dol`, `dół` | `pitchdown` | expression | Pitch the nose down (3D only) |
| `pp`, `przechylprawo` | `rr`, `rollright` | expression | Roll to the right around the heading (3D only) |
| `pl`, `przechyllewo` | `rl`, `rollleft` | expression | Roll to the left (3D only) |

Every Polish and English alias is equivalent. `nrpowt` (alias `repcount`) is a value, not a command: see Repeat.

### Expressions

- Wherever a command takes an expression, it accepts a number, a name (a parameter or a variable, also in the legacy form `:name`), `nrpowt`, a parenthesised expression, a unary `-` or `+` applied to any of these, or two expressions joined by `+`, `-`, `*` or `/`.
- `*` and `/` bind tighter than `+` and `-`; operators of equal precedence associate to the left: `np 20 - 5 - 3` moves 12 and `np 2 + 3 * 4` moves 14.
- A binary operator must have whitespace on both sides or on neither side. `np 10 - 5` and `np 10-5` both move 5. `np 10 -5` is `np 10` followed by the stray token `-5`, which is an error, because the `-` has whitespace only on its left. The same rule applies to `+`, `*` and `/`. The rule does not apply to comparisons.
- Unary signs may be stacked and applied anywhere an operand is expected: `np -(3 - 5)`, `np - -2`, `np -bok`.
- Division by zero and any non-finite result are run-time errors. Evaluating an expression is not an executed operation (see Limits).
- A condition is `expression comparison expression`. Comparisons are exact: `jeśli 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 [...]` does not run its body.

### Turtle and geometry

- Coordinates are right-handed: +X to the right, +Y forward on the page, +Z up out of the page. The 2D plane is the XY plane (z = 0).
- The turtle starts at the origin (0, 0, 0), heading +Y, with its right side along +X and its up vector along +Z, pen down, colour `#16866a`, width 3.
- `np d` moves the turtle `d` units along its heading; `ws d` moves it `-d`. If the pen is down and the position changes, a straight segment from the old to the new position is drawn with the current colour and width. A move of zero draws nothing.
- `pw a` rotates the heading `a` degrees to the right around the turtle's up vector (clockwise when seen from above); `lw a` rotates left. The right vector follows the heading.
- `gora a` rotates the heading `a` degrees towards the up vector around the right vector (the up vector follows, so after `gora 90` the turtle heads along its former up); `dol a` rotates the opposite way.
- `pp a` rotates the turtle's up vector `a` degrees towards its right vector, around the heading (the right vector follows, so after `pp 90` the turtle's up is its former right and its right is its former down); `pl a` rotates the opposite way. The heading does not change.
- In 2D mode, `gora`, `dol`, `pp` and `pl` are errors.
- Angles are in degrees, any decimal value; negative values turn the other way.
- `dom` moves the turtle to the origin, drawing a segment if the pen is down and the turtle is not already there, then sets the heading to +Y, the right vector to +X and the up vector to +Z. Pen state, colour and width are untouched.
- `czyść` removes every segment drawn so far and changes nothing else: `run` then returns only the segments drawn afterwards. The segment limit (see Limits) counts the segments currently kept.
- Pen state, colour and width persist until changed. Programs made only of flat commands produce identical coordinates in 2D and 3D mode.

### Repeat

`powtorz n [ ... ]` runs the bracketed commands `n` times; `n` must evaluate to an integer from 0 to 10000 (0 runs nothing). Bodies may contain any commands, nested repeats, conditionals and procedure calls.

Inside a repeat body, `nrpowt` is the number of the current iteration of the innermost enclosing repeat, starting at 1. The enclosing repeat is found lexically: `nrpowt` written in a procedure body that is not itself inside a repeat is a parse-time error, even if the procedure is only ever called from inside a repeat. `nrpowt` written outside any repeat at top level is a parse-time error too.

### Variables

- `niech x 5` assigns the value of the expression to the variable `x`; any later `niech x ...` reassigns it. Variable names follow the rules for procedure names and may not be command words or the name of a procedure.
- A `niech` at top level creates or updates a global variable. A `niech` inside a procedure creates or updates a variable local to that call; it shadows a global of the same name for the rest of the call and is discarded when the call ends. A parameter can be reassigned the same way.
- A name may be used in an expression only if it is a parameter of the enclosing procedure, or is assigned by `niech` somewhere in the body of the enclosing procedure, or is assigned by `niech` somewhere at top level (before or after the use). Any other name is a parse-time error.
- Reading a declared variable that has not been assigned yet on the current path is a run-time error, reported at the first token of the argument that contains the reference.

### Conditionals

`jeśli warunek [ ... ]` runs the body when the condition holds. `jeżeli warunek [ ... ] [ ... ]` runs the first body when it holds and the second otherwise. Bodies may contain anything a repeat body may contain. Conditional bodies count towards the bracket nesting limit but are not execution frames.

### Procedures

```logo
oto kwadrat ma: bok, kąt
  powtorz 4 [np bok pw kąt]
już

kwadrat 80 90
```

- A definition starts with `oto` (alias `to`) at the beginning of a line, followed on the same line by the name and, optionally, `ma:` and a comma-separated parameter list. The body follows on the next lines and ends with `już` (aliases `juz`, `end`) alone on its own line.
- The legacy header `oto kwadrat :bok :kąt` is also accepted, and a parameter may be referenced in the body as `:bok` as well as plainly as `bok`.
- Calls take positional arguments separated by whitespace, exactly as many as the procedure has parameters; each argument is an expression, so `kwadrat 40 * 2 90` passes 80 and 90. A parameter may share its name with a procedure: in command position the name is a call, in argument position it is the parameter.
- Parameters and local variables are local to the call and can stand in for any expression, including repeat counts and arguments of other procedure calls.
- Definitions are top-level only (never inside a repeat body, a conditional body or another procedure) and may appear before or after the calls that use them. A name may be defined once.
- Procedures may call themselves, directly or through other procedures. `stop` ends the current call immediately; at top level it ends the program. A `stop` inside a repeat or conditional body ends the enclosing procedure call (or the program), not just the body.
- There are no return values.

### Errors and limits

- Any problem is reported with the 1-based line and column of the offending token: an unknown command, a missing or malformed argument, a malformed colour, a width outside 1–12 or not an integer, a repeat count outside 0–10000 or not an integer, an unbalanced bracket or parenthesis, a procedure call with the wrong number of arguments, a definition inside a body, a missing `już`, a name that is neither a parameter nor a declared variable, `nrpowt` outside a repeat, a pitch or roll command in 2D mode, division by zero, an unassigned variable, or a limit exceeded.
- An invalid argument (a bad width or repeat count, a division by zero, a non-finite result, an unassigned variable) is reported at the first token of that argument's expression, not at the command. A missing argument is reported at the token found where the argument should have started (for example a `]` or `)`), or at the command itself when the program ends there. A stray value where a command is expected is reported at that value.
- A program is validated as a whole before anything is drawn: with a parse-time error nothing is drawn. Widths and repeat counts written as literal expressions (no names) are checked at parse time; those that depend on names are checked when executed. Errors that can only be found while running (a limit exceeded, division by zero, an unassigned variable, a bad width or repeat count computed from a name) stop execution and keep what was drawn so far, after any `czyść` that ran.
- Limits: 50,000 source characters, 10,000 tokens (operators, parentheses, brackets and commas are tokens), nesting depth 32 for brackets, 32 active procedure-call and repeat frames at any moment (conditional bodies do not count), 10,000 executed operations counting each command, each `niech`, each conditional, each repeat and each call, plus one for finishing each repeat iteration, conditional body or procedure call (reaching the end of the program is not counted), 10,000 kept segments, and every coordinate within ±100,000. Exceeding a limit is an error.

=== END SPECIFICATION ===

content.text: Now the main application module: state, studio, routing, and the testing hook.

The suite is written and run: **407 tests, 406 pass, 1 fail.** The one failure is a real bug in the implementation, not in the test.

**Implementation bug found**
- **Program:** `np 1 niech x` (the program ends right after the variable name)
- **Expected (spec):** "A missing argument is reported at the token found where the argument should have started …, or at the command itself when the program ends there." So the error should be at line 1, column 6, the `niech`.
- **Actual:** the error is at line 1, column 12, the name `x`. The message is "Po „niech x” brakuje wartości…". When the value is missing before a `]` (e.g. `powtorz 2 [niech x]`), the error is correctly at the `]`.

**Tests I got wrong and fixed after re-reading the spec**
- **Too many arguments, definition after the call:** in `p 1 2 3` with a two-parameter `p`, the stray value is the `3` at column 7, not column 5.
- **`np (10 -5)`:** the implementation reports the unclosed `(` at column 4. The spec allows either the `(` (an unbalanced parenthesis) or the stray `-`, so the test now accepts column 4 or 8 and still requires a parse-time error.
- **Variable named after a procedure:** the implementation reports whichever name comes first in the source, so it may point at the definition's name rather than the `niech`. The spec doesn't say which token is the offending one, so the test now only checks for a parse-time error, in both orders.

**What's covered**
- **Lexical rules:** case-insensitivity, accented and unaccented aliases, comments, number formats (`1e3`, `0x10`, `NaN`, `Infinity` rejected), colour literals and 10 malformed colour forms.
- **Commands:** every alias of every command, including the 3D ones. Pitch and roll are parse-time errors in 2D.
- **Expressions:** precedence and associativity, the whitespace rule for all four operators (including `np 10 -5` at the `-`, column 7), stacked unary signs, division by zero and non-finite results (run-time, at the argument), exact comparisons.
- **Geometry:** pitch, roll and turn combinations in 3D exactly as the spec describes them, `dom`, `czyść`, and identical results in 2D and 3D for flat programs.
- **Control flow and procedures:** repeat and `nrpowt` (including the lexical parse-time rule), variables and scoping, conditionals, both procedure header forms, arity errors, recursion, `stop` semantics, and all the definition errors.
- **Limits:** characters, tokens, bracket nesting and frames at their exact boundaries; operation counting only at unambiguous boundaries. The examples test passes: all 13 standard programs run without error and draw something.

**Limits I could only partly test**
- **10,000 kept segments:** this can't be exceeded without first exceeding the 10,000-operation or 10,000-token limit, so I only test that a 9,980-segment drawing works.
- **Commas as tokens:** not tested exactly, because the spec doesn't say whether `ma:` (or `:a`) counts as one token or two, which makes an exact boundary impossible.
- **Coordinate overflow:** tested by line and by the earlier segments being kept. Whether the column points at the command or at its argument, and whether the overflowing segment itself is drawn, is left open because the spec doesn't say.

Files are in /work/tests:
- helpers.ts
- lexical.test.ts
- commands.test.ts
- expressions.test.ts
- geometry.test.ts
- control.test.ts
- procedures.test.ts
- limits.test.ts
- misc.test.ts
- examples.test.ts

input.command:
cd /tmp/debs && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re,subprocess,os
want="fonts-dejavu-core fonts-liberation2 fontconfig-config libfontconfig1 libfreetype6 libpng16-16 libbrotli1 fonts-noto-mono".split()
pk={}
for block in open('Packages',encoding='utf-8',errors='replace').read().split('\n\n'):
    m=re.search(r'^Package: (.+)$',block,re.M); f=re.search(r'^Filename: (.+)$',block,re.M)
    if m and f: pk[m.group(1)]=f.group(1)
for w in want:
    if w in pk: subprocess.run(['curl','-sSfL','-o',os.path.basename(pk[w]),'http://deb.debian.org/debian/'+pk[w]])
    else: print('missing',w)
EOF
for f in fonts-*.deb fontconfig*.deb libfontconfig*.deb libfreetype*.deb libpng*.deb libbrotli*.deb; do dpkg-deb -x "$f" root; done
mkdir -p /tmp/fc-cache && cat > /tmp/debs/fonts.conf <<'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "fonts.dtd">
<fontconfig>
  <dir>/tmp/debs/root/usr/share/fonts</dir>
  <cachedir>/tmp/fc-cache</cachedir>
  <config></config>
</fontconfig>
EOF
find root/usr/share/fonts -name "*.ttf" | head -5

input.content:
# Logomocja

Polskie studio Logo z żółwiem, który rysuje na płaszczyźnie (2D) i w przestrzeni (3D).
Inspiracją jest klasyczna polska Logomocja; to jej współczesna, przeglądarkowa wersja:
działa na komputerze i telefonie, bez kont, bez serwera i bez sieci.

## Uruchamianie

Wymagany jest [Bun](https://bun.sh) (1.1 lub nowszy).

```sh
bun install          # zależności
bun run dev          # serwer deweloperski Vite (http://localhost:5173)
bun run build        # statyczna strona w dist/
bun run preview      # podgląd zbudowanej strony
bun run test         # testy interpretera i treści (bun test)
bun run typecheck    # sprawdzenie typów TypeScript
```

### Budowanie pod podścieżką

`bun run build` honoruje zmienną `BASE_PATH` (domyślnie `/`). Strona w `dist/` to zwykłe

podstrony działa na każdym statycznym hostingu, także bez reguł przepisywania adresów:

```sh
# zawartość dist/ można teraz serwować spod /Logomocja/builds/x/
```

- **Studio**: edytor z numerami wierszy, kolorowaniem składni, znacznikiem błędu
  (wiersz, kolumna, komunikat po polsku) i podświetleniem wykonywanego wiersza.
  Przyciski Uruchom, Krok, Pauza/Wznów, Reset i suwak tempa. Edycja w trakcie
  działania zatrzymuje program, ale zostawia to, co już narysowano.
- **Widok 2D** (płótno): przesuwanie, powiększanie (kółko, gest, klawisze), dopasowanie,

  i pokazuje uproszczony, nieruchomy rzut aksonometryczny, a tryb 2D działa normalnie.

  we właściwym trybie. Jeśli w szkicu jest własny program, aplikacja pyta o zgodę
  i zachowuje kopię, którą można przywrócić.
- **Wyzwania**: 9 zadań (7 w 2D, 2 w 3D) z automatycznym sprawdzaniem. Sprawdzarka porównuje
  kształt i rozmiar rysunku ze wzorem: nie liczy się kolejność ani kierunek rysowania,
  podział odcinków ani położenie całości. Tolerancja to 1% rozmiaru wzoru, co najmniej

  przeładowanie strony.

| Skrót | Działanie |
| --- | --- |
| Ctrl/⌘ + Enter | Uruchom |
| Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + Enter, F10 | Krok |
| Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + Spacja, F8 | Pauza / wznów |
| Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + X | Reset |
| Tab / Esc, Tab (w edytorze) | wcięcie / wyjście z edytora |
| strzałki, +, −, 0 (na rysunku) | przesuwanie (2D) lub obracanie (3D), powiększanie, dopasowanie |

Po załadowaniu strony dostępny jest obiekt `window.logomocja`:

- `version`: wersja z `package.json`,
- `run(source, mode)`: interpretuje program bez dotykania interfejsu i zwraca
  `{ segments, error }`,
- `open(source, mode)`: wkleja program do edytora w danym trybie, wykonuje go bez animacji,
  dopasowuje widok i zwraca obietnicę z `{ segments, error }`, gdy rysunek jest już na ekranie,
- dodatkowo `examples` (lista przykładów) i `loadExample(nazwa)`.

`mode` to `"2d"` albo `"3d"`. Odcinek ma postać
`{ from: [x, y, z], to: [x, y, z], color: "#rrggbb", width }`, a błąd postać
`{ message, line, column }` (kolumna i wiersz liczone od 1).

## Struktura projektu

```
src/lang/        interpreter: lekser, parser (pełna walidacja przed uruchomieniem), wykonanie z limitami
src/content/     przykłady, wyzwania i sprawdzarka, treść pomocy
src/ui/          edytor, widoki 2D i 3D, odtwarzacz animacji, strony, udostępnianie, motyw
src/styles.css   wygląd (jasny i ciemny motyw, układ na telefon i komputer)
tests/           testy (bun test): specyfikacja języka, limity, programy standardowe, wyzwania, pomoc
```

Interpreter najpierw analizuje cały program. Błąd składni oznacza, że nic nie zostanie
narysowane. Potem program się wykonuje i zapisuje ślad kroków, który odtwarzacz animuje
(z płynnym ruchem żółwia przy wolnym tempie). Błąd wykonania zatrzymuje program,
a narysowane odcinki zostają.

### Rozstrzygnięcia niejednoznaczności

- Licznik operacji: zakończenie obrotu pętli albo bloku warunku liczy się tylko wtedy,
  gdy blok dobiegł końca. Blok przerwany przez `stop` się nie liczy. Zakończenie wywołania
  procedury liczy się zawsze, także po `stop`.
- Ramka `powtórz` (do limitu 32) powstaje także przy zerowej liczbie powtórzeń.
- Przekroczenie limitu współrzędnych, odcinków lub operacji jest zgłaszane przy poleceniu,
  które by go przekroczyło. Takie polecenie niczego już nie rysuje.
- Nawiasy okrągłe można zagnieżdżać najwyżej na 32 poziomy, tak jak kwadratowe.
- Szerokość i liczba powtórzeń zapisane samymi liczbami są sprawdzane przed uruchomieniem.
  Dzielenie przez zero w takim zapisie jest jednak zawsze błędem wykonania.
- Kolor można zapisać także w polskich cudzysłowach („…”), bo telefony często zamieniają
  nimi zwykłe cudzysłowy.

input.prompt:
Review the browser UI code of a small web app in /work for real bugs. Do not modify any files; report findings only.

Context: /work is "Logomocja", a Polish Logo turtle-drawing studio (TypeScript, Vite, three.js). The interpreter lives in /work/src/lang (well tested — out of scope unless a UI file misuses it). The UI is in /work/src/ui (app.ts is the controller: contexts/drafts, routing via location.hash, playback, challenges, file open/download, permalinks, testing hook; editor.ts is a textarea + highlighted overlay editor; player.ts animates a precomputed execution trace; view2d.ts/paint.ts draw on canvas; view3d.ts uses three.js; pages.ts renders the examples/challenges/reference pages; overlay.ts has dialogs/toasts; share.ts encodes permalinks; storage.ts wraps localStorage), plus /work/src/main.ts and /work/src/styles.css.

Product requirements that the UI must satisfy (check these specifically):
- Run, step command-by-command, pause, resume, reset; a speed control; the line being executed is highlighted while running or stepping; editing while a program runs is handled sensibly.
- Errors show line+column and Polish message inline in the editor; a parse-time error draws nothing; a run-time error keeps what was drawn.
- 2D view: pan, zoom, fit, visible origin. 3D view: orbit, pan, zoom, reset, grid, axes; if WebGL is unavailable the 2D part must still work and the app must say why 3D is off.
- Loading an example must not silently destroy the user's unsaved draft. Drafts for each mode survive reload (localStorage only).
- Permalink encodes program+mode in the URL; opening it loads and runs the program. PNG export; download/open .logo files.
- Keyboard shortcuts for run/step/pause/reset; every control keyboard-operable and labelled; visible focus; light/dark theme following system with manual toggle; usable on phones.

content.text:
I found 12 real issues in `/work/src/ui`; the two worst can lose user drafts without warning. I didn't modify any files. `tsc --noEmit` passes, `bun test tests` passes (453/453), and a build with `BASE_PATH=/sub/dir` emits correct asset URLs. Hash routing and permalinks keep the sub-path, so the BASE_PATH requirement is met.

## High

**1. Multi-tab overwrite loses drafts and challenge progress.** `/work/src/ui/app.ts:222`, `:257-264`
- `persistNow()` writes both drafts, all challenge progress and the context, and it runs every time a tab is hidden. Nothing listens for the `storage` event.
- Scenario: tab B is open with draft X. The user edits X into Y in tab A, which gets saved. They glance at tab B and switch away. Tab B now writes its stale X over Y, and any challenges solved in A lose their solved flag and code.
- Fix: only write keys that changed (a dirty flag per buffer), and handle `storage` events to refresh the in-memory buffers, or at least to stop writing stale ones.

**2. Opening permalinks can destroy the draft through the single backup slot.** `app.ts:627` together with `:903-913` (`kod` route, `confirm: false`)
- Each permalink silently moves the current draft into `backup:<mode>`, overwriting whatever backup was there.
- Scenario: the user has draft D and opens link L1, so the backup is D. They open link L2 (in any tab), and L1 now counts as a user draft, so the backup becomes L1. D is gone with no dialog.
- Fix: ask for confirmation when the draft would be replaced and the backup slot is already full, or keep a small backup stack. Never overwrite a backup with content that itself came from a link or a load.

## Medium

**3. Stale run after the async 3D load.** `app.ts:416-439` (`startExec`, `runAction`, `stepAction`), `:459-473` (`runInstant`), `:784-797` (`checkCurrent`)

- Scenario: switch to 3D, press Ctrl+Enter, then click "Szkic 2D" or edit the code before three.js arrives. The old 3D program then plays in the 2D view, highlighting lines of a program that is no longer in the editor.
- In `checkCurrent`, switching context during the await means the verdict uses the new context's editor text. If that passes, it is saved as challenge `ch`'s code.
- Fix: add a run-generation counter, bumped in `applyContext`, `onEdit`, `resetAction` and each new run. After every await, bail out if the counter or mode changed. In `checkCurrent`, capture the source before awaiting.

**4. The skip link is treated as a route.** `/work/index.html:23` with `app.ts:916`
- `href="#main"` sets the hash to `main`, which hits the `default:` case: `replaceState('#/')` and `showPage('studio')`.

- Fix: in a click handler, call `preventDefault()` and `main.focus()`, or have the router ignore hashes that don't start with `#/`.

**5. Changing the theme re-runs the router.** `app.ts:943-949`
- `void this.route()` runs on every theme change, including automatic system switches.
- On Pomoc it calls `renderReferencePage`, which scrolls to the top or to the section in the URL, so the reading position is lost.
- On Przykłady, all cards are rebuilt and any open "Pokaż kod" sections collapse.
- If the hash is `#/przyklad/x` while the replace-draft confirm dialog is open, a system theme flip calls `loadExample` again and stacks a second dialog.
- Reference thumbnails are never repainted, because `renderedReference` stays true, so they keep the old theme's background.
- `renderChallengeCard()` also wipes the "Zaliczone / Jeszcze nie" result.
- Fix: repaint thumbnails in place (re-run `paintThumbnail` on existing canvases) instead of re-routing.

**6. The 3D view churns the GPU during animation.** `/work/src/ui/view3d.ts:261-314`
- The partial segment's geometry and `LineMaterial` are destroyed and recreated on every frame.
- The whole drawing is rebuilt and re-uploaded whenever the segment count changes, which is O(n²) over a run.
- When all old line materials are disposed in the same frame, three.js's `releaseProgram` reaches `usedTimes === 0` and deletes the line shader. It is recompiled on the next render. This happens on every frame where a segment completes, and on every frame while only the partial line exists.
- Fix: keep one persistent partial line and update its positions. Grow the drawing incrementally, or preallocate and use `instanceCount`.

## Low

7. **A Run parse error gets downgraded to a hint.** `app.ts:402-411` vs `:558`. A pending `liveTimer` from typing fires after Ctrl+Enter. The "Błąd – nic nie narysowano" error becomes "Uwaga", and the red line bar disappears. Fix: `clearTimeout(this.liveTimer)` in `prepareRun` and `runInstant`.
8. **Focus order doesn't match the layout.** `app.ts:205`. The DOM order is stage pane then editor pane, but the desktop grid puts the editor on the left. Tab therefore reaches Run, the canvas and view tools before the editor. Fix: put the editor first in the DOM and use `order` / grid areas to place it.
9. **F10 and F8 are hijacked even with Shift.** `app.ts:964-965`. Shift+F10 is the standard keyboard way to open a context menu, and this blocks it. Fix: add `!e.shiftKey`.
10. **The theme-color meta is never updated.** `app.ts:947`. `meta[name="theme-color"]:not([media])` matches nothing, because both tags in `index.html` have `media`. A manual theme toggle never updates the mobile browser bar.
11. **WebGL probe and fallback message.**
    - `webgl.ts` / `app.ts:68`: `webglAvailable()` leaves a live probe context behind. Release it with `WEBGL_lose_context`.
    - `app.ts:327-331`: a network failure loading the view3d chunk is reported as "Nie udało się uruchomić WebGL", and the fallback is cached for the whole session.
12. **A malformed `%` in the hash breaks routing.** `app.ts:862`. For example, `#/pomoc/%` makes `decodeURIComponent` throw, `route()` rejects without handling, and the page doesn't change. Fix: wrap it in try/catch.

## Checked and OK

- **`open()`** meets the requirements: it loads, runs without animation, fits, waits two frames plus a synchronous paint, and returns `exec.segments` and the error in the same shape as `run()`. Its only weakness is the race in item 3, and it never resolves in a hidden tab, because `nextPaint` relies on `requestAnimationFrame`.
- **`window.logomocja.run`** does not touch the UI.
- **Editor overlay alignment**: font, padding, tab size, line height and scroll sync all match the textarea.
- **Mid-run behaviour**: editing during a run halts it, a parse error clears the drawing, a run-time error keeps it, and switching modes mid-animation clears the player.
- **Example loading** asks before replacing a draft and keeps a backup.
- **3D object disposal** frees geometry, materials and textures, so nothing leaks.

content.text:
Logomocja is built and working in `/work`. `bun install`, `bun run build` and `bun run test` all succeed from a clean copy, and all 453 tests pass. I checked it in a headless Chromium on desktop and phone sizes, in light and dark themes, and with WebGL turned off. Nothing has been committed to git.

**What a learner gets**
- **Studio:** an editor with line numbers, syntax colouring, an inline Polish error marker at the exact line and column, and the line being executed highlighted. Buttons for run, step, pause/resume and reset, plus a speed slider; the turtle glides at slow speeds.
- **Editing while running:** the program stops, keeps what it has drawn, and a message asks you to run it again.
- **Live syntax check:** errors are flagged while you type.
- **2D view:** pan, zoom, fit, an origin marker and a labelled grid.
- **3D view:** three.js, loaded only when first needed. Orbit, pan, zoom, reset, ground grid and axes, and a turtle whose roll you can see. Without WebGL the app explains why 3D is off and shows a still, simplified projection instead.
- **The 13 standard programs:** shipped as given. They load by name (`#/przyklad/kula`) into the right mode. Replacing a draft of your own asks first and keeps the old version so you can restore it.
- **9 challenges:** 7 in 2D and 2 in 3D, checked automatically. Shape and size must match; drawing order, direction and starting position don't matter. Failures come with a reason, for example "Rozmiar się nie zgadza…" or "lustrzane odbicie…". Progress is saved locally.
- **Sharing and files:** permalinks that load and run the program, PNG export, and saving/opening `.logo` files.
- **Help page:** full reference in Polish, with a runnable example and thumbnail for every command.
- **Shortcuts:** Ctrl+Enter run, Ctrl+Shift+Enter or F10 step, Ctrl+Shift+Space or F8 pause/resume, Ctrl+Shift+X reset.
- **Accessibility:** light, dark and system theme, keyboard access to every control, visible focus, and a bottom tab bar on phones.
- **Testing hook:** `window.logomocja` provides `version`, `run(source, mode)` and `open(source, mode)`.
- **Sub-path builds:** `BASE_PATH=/Logomocja/builds/x/` works when served from that sub-path, including refreshing on any page.

**How it was checked**
- **Interpreter tests:** a separate agent wrote 407 tests from the language spec alone. They found one bug: a missing `niech` value at the end of a program was reported at the wrong token. I fixed it.
- **UI review:** a second agent reviewed the UI code and found 12 real problems, all now fixed. The worst two could lose a draft: a tab left open in the background could overwrite newer work saved in another tab, and opening two shared links in a row could push out the oldest saved draft. I re-tested each fixed case in the browser.

**Where the spec was ambiguous, I chose:**
- **Operation counting with `stop`:** a loop pass or `jeśli` body cut short by `stop` doesn't count as "finished", but a procedure call ended by `stop` does.
- **Error positions:**
  - an unclosed `[` is reported at that `[`;
  - a missing `już` is reported at the `oto`;
  - going past the coordinate, segment or operation limit is reported at the command that would cross it, and that command draws nothing.
- **Extra limit:** parentheses can nest at most 32 deep, the same as square brackets.

These are all listed in the README and the help page.

Everything is in `/work`: `src/lang` is the interpreter, `src/ui` the app, `src/content` the examples, challenges and help text, and `tests/` the test suite.
